Microsoft Cost Management is a suite of tools within Microsoft Azure designed for monitoring, analyzing, allocating, and optimizing costs across Microsoft Cloud workloads and Azure services. It enables users to track and control spending by setting budgets, creating cost alerts, detecting anomalies, and generating detailed cost reports. The tool supports cost forecasting, cost pattern analysis, and organization-wide cost governance.

Microsoft Cost Management provides granular cost tracking across various resource types, including compute, storage, backup, licensing, function apps, and database resources. It allows users to organize and filter costs by resource, environment, business unit, and customer, supporting scenarios such as disaster recovery tier management and per-customer cost tracking. The tool encourages consistent tagging across resources for effective cost allocation, enabling chargeback and showback reporting by aggregating and filtering costs based on tag values.<SEP>Microsoft Cost Management is a tool for understanding and managing Azure spending.<SEP>Microsoft Cost Management provides tools for cost governance including cost analysis, budgets, and cost alerts.<SEP>Microsoft Cost Management is a tool used to monitor and optimize spending for Azure Virtual Desktop.

Azure Reservations is a cost-saving pricing mechanism offered by Microsoft Azure that allows customers to prepay for compute and other resources by committing to one-year or three-year plans. By making this commitment, customers receive significant billing discounts compared to standard consumption-based (pay-as-you-go) pricing.

Azure Reservations are particularly well-suited for stable, predictable workloads that exist for extended periods with consistent usage patterns. They provide reserved capacity across multiple Azure products, automatically applying discounts to matching resources. Additionally, Azure Reservations can be used as a strategy for reducing costs even in ephemeral environments.<SEP>Azure reservations allow maximizing cost efficiency for customers with long-term commitments and guaranteed compute utilization.

The Sharding pattern is an Azure architecture pattern providing guidance on horizontal partitioning.<SEP>A data distribution pattern that ensures even distribution of data across partitions using a shard key.<SEP>Sharding pattern is an architectural pattern for partitioning data across multiple databases.

A cloud storage service with limits on the volume of requests a single partition can handle.<SEP>Azure Table Storage is a secure shared storage option for agent state persistence.<SEP>Azure Table Storage is a simpler, lower-cost option for read-heavy workloads in batch inference scenarios.

The data attribute or combination of attributes that determines which shard contains a particular data item, also known as a partition key.<SEP>A key used in horizontal partitioning to ensure even data distribution and efficient query routing.

Offline migration involves making partitions unavailable while relocating data to reduce the chance of issues during rebalancing.<SEP>Offline migration is a data migration technique where partitions are made unavailable during data relocation to reduce contention.

Online migration involves migrating data between partitions while they are still in use.<SEP>Online migration is a data migration technique that is more complex but less disruptive, allowing data access during migration from original and new partitions.
Shard rebalancing periodically redistributes data by size and workload to minimize hotspots and maximize query performance.
Cross-partition joins are inefficient query operations that join data across multiple partitions, typically requiring consecutive queries based on keys and foreign keys.
Static reference data such as postal code tables or product lists can be replicated across all partitions to reduce separate lookup operations.
Referential integrity across partitions must be maintained by the application logic rather than the data store in vertical and functional partitioning schemes.
Index Table pattern is an architectural pattern for efficient data querying.
Materialized View pattern is an architectural pattern for precomputed query results.

Elastic Pools are a feature of Azure SQL Database that allow managing, scaling, and sharing resources across multiple databases within a single resource pool on a single server. They are a cost-effective solution for workloads with varying usage demands, commonly used in SaaS solutions.

Elastic Pools support horizontal scaling by partitioning data into shards spread across multiple databases, reducing contention. A shardlet is a dataset within a shard, which can be a single data item or group of items sharing the same shardlet key.<SEP>A shardlet is a unit of data within a shard, which can be range-based or list-based.

The sharding key determines how data is distributed across shards; choosing the right key is critical for even workload distribution.

A separate SQL database that acts as a global manager maintaining a list of all shards and shardlets in the system.

A sharding scheme that associates a single key with a shardlet, providing isolation by holding each shardlet in its own shard.
A sharding scheme that associates contiguous key values with a shardlet, less expensive but providing less isolation than list shard maps.

Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) is a cloud-based desktop and application virtualization service that runs on Microsoft Azure, providing a managed Microsoft control plane for virtual desktop infrastructure. It enables organizations to deploy, manage, and maintain virtual desktop workloads, giving users access to their desktops and applications from anywhere, on any device. AVD supports Windows 10/11 Enterprise multi-session remote desktops and offers features like pooled resources, personal desktops, autoscaling, and hybrid environments. It serves as a cost-effective modernization path for Remote Desktop Services by migrating end-user desktops to the cloud.

AVD manages session hosts, host pools, and application groups, with operators using scaling plans and load balancing algorithms to manage workloads. It operates within Azure capacity limits under a shared responsibility model between Microsoft and customers, requiring collaboration between platform and workload teams. The service encompasses performance, operational, and security considerations, including access control, diagnostics, and security monitoring capabilities. Its components require version compliance and regular updates.

For security, AVD uses TLS 1.2 for secure connections and supports hybrid identities, cloud-only identities, and various security configurations. It leverages FSLogix for user profile management and App Attach for application delivery to session hosts. AVD provides comprehensive networking guidance covering traffic optimization, network security, segmentation, multi-region connectivity, and hybrid networking, requiring real-time, low-latency network connectivity for a seamless user experience. It can be deployed on Azure Local and serves as an alternative to traditional VMs in policy-restricted environments.

GenAIOps, or Generative Artificial Intelligence Operations, is a methodology and set of operational practices focused on the lifecycle management of generative AI solutions. It is considered a specialized subset of MLOps that extends beyond traditional machine learning operations to address the unique requirements of generative AI workloads.

GenAIOps encompasses practices for discovering, evaluating, integrating, and deploying generative AI models. Key activities include selecting the right model, prompt engineering, prompt iteration, fine-tuning pretrained models with enriched data, and incorporating domain-specific knowledge through techniques such as Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). These practices are integrated into broader DevOps and CI/CD processes.

GenAIOps also serves as a maturity framework, particularly within Azure Machine Learning, where maturity levels progress from basic model usage to structured deployment leveraging automated optimization techniques. It is relevant to SaaS businesses and organizations implementing generative AI strategies at scale.

Responsible AI is a comprehensive framework and set of principles aimed at ensuring the ethical, fair, transparent, and inclusive design, deployment, and use of AI systems. It serves as both a primary design driver and a referenced resource, addressing safety measures and controls alongside traditional application security considerations.

Responsible AI provides guidance for the responsible deployment of AI systems, including safeguards for agentic AI, content safety, and broader ethical considerations. As a design area related to security principles, Responsible AI emphasizes user experience and the ethical implications of releasing AI solutions to the public. Its principles guide organizations to align AI usage with brand values and industry standards, ensuring that AI algorithms operate safely and avoid unintended harm.

nodes.description:
The General Purpose tier is a compute and service tier offered across multiple Azure database services, designed to provide balanced cost-performance for standard production workloads requiring consistent performance.

In Azure Database for MySQL, the General Purpose tier supports workloads needing high availability (HA), read replicas, and accelerated logs, offering balanced compute and memory resources for production environments. However, failovers in this tier involve cold-cache performance degradation, as the instance restarts on a new node without warm replicas.

In Azure SQL Managed Instance, the General Purpose tier tolerates higher storage latency and uses remote storage with file-size-dependent IOPS. It provides lower per-vCore TempDB allocation compared to higher tiers. This tier supports stop/start functionality, including stop/start schedules, and offers favorable Azure Hybrid Benefit conversion ratios.

nodes.description: Elasticsearch is a powerful search index technology recommended for indexing grounding data.<SEP>Elasticsearch is a search index technology providing powerful search capabilities including vectorized and relevancy-based searches.<SEP>Elasticsearch is a search index technology that provides powerful search capabilities including vectorized and relevancy-based searches, as well as preprocessing features during index creation.

Data preparation is the process of cleaning, transforming, and structuring grounding data to reduce noise and bias, search efficiently, and maximize relevancy of index searches.
Data volume rescoping involves adjusting the scope of data by expanding or narrowing it to create a tight index so that relevance and query efficiency are increased.

Chunking is a technique related to breaking data into meaningful segments that align with the context window size of a model.<SEP>Chunking involves dividing text into smaller pieces that can be individually processed and indexed for efficient search and retrieval.
A context window refers to the maximum amount of text that a model can handle at one time when generating a response.
Enriching is a process of augmenting context by adding extra information to grounding data to make it more meaningful, such as generating relevant questions or tagging content with metadata.
Data type morphing involves converting source data types to functional data types that help in querying and analysis, such as converting images into vector representations.

Grounding data is sourced from data platforms and indexed with context so that models can give relevant responses.<SEP>Grounding data is information provided to a language model at inference time to help it generate more accurate and relevant responses, supplementing data not part of original training.<SEP>Grounding data is existing data that needs to be made suitable for semantic querying to support inferencing requests to a model.<SEP>Grounding data is the information provided to a model as context for generating responses, often containing large volumes of information.<SEP>Grounding data involves data sources, ownership, refresh frequency, and bias elimination processes used alongside model training.<SEP>Grounding data is preprocessed, chunked, and indexed data that seeds generative AI models to improve relevance.
Semantic querying is a method of searching data based on meaning and context rather than just literal matching.

Data lineage involves tracking the source of data to maintain transparency and accountability for internal data governance teams.<SEP>Data lineage provides a clear record of data processing stages to support auditability and transparency in decision-making.<SEP>Data lineage refers to tracking the path of data from its source to its use in model training, essential for explainability, debugging, and detecting biases.
Vector representations are numerical encodings of data such as images that enable efficient semantic searches and comparisons.
Full-document grounding is a strategy where the entire text is fed directly to the model, improving accuracy but increasing token costs.
Embeddings are mathematical representations of objects generated by AI models that enable vector search capabilities and improve query relevancy.

Index maintenance is a crucial aspect of index design involving data management over time, including handling changes and updates.<SEP>Index maintenance is the ongoing process of updating, adding, and deleting data and fields in an index over time.

The right to be forgotten refers to an individual's right to have their personal data removed from online platforms or databases.<SEP>RTBF is a procedure for handling user requests to have their data removed, relevant to responsible AI policies.<SEP>RTBF (Right to Be Forgotten) is a compliance requirement ensuring user data can be deleted upon request.<SEP>The right to be forgotten refers to an individual's right to have their personal data removed from platforms or databases, requiring policies for removing personal training data.
Side-by-side deployments involve creating a new updated index alongside the existing one, then switching queries after testing.
Forward compatibility is a mindset for index design that ensures schema changes do not disrupt application functionality.
Generative AI models are prebuilt or pretrained models that can be augmented with context-specific data to improve performance for specific workload requirements.

nodes.description:
Azure VMware Solution is a Microsoft managed cloud service that enables organizations to migrate and run on-premises VMware vSphere workloads on Azure infrastructure, integrating VMware vSphere hypervisor with Azure dedicated BareMetal infrastructure. It provides a private cloud platform for hosting, deploying, and managing applications and workloads using virtual machines, including back-end APIs and applications, leveraging both VMware and Microsoft proprietary services.

The service offers comprehensive software-defined data center (SDDC) capabilities, including compute, storage, and networking, along with DNS and IP management features. It supports clustering and high availability through stretched cluster capabilities across availability zones. Azure VMware Solution integrates with various Azure services, VMware SDDC components, and monitoring tools, providing robust monitoring and security capabilities.

Infrastructure management encompasses backups, disaster recovery, operations management, incident response, and well-architected networking for connectivity, performance, and availability. The platform requires security measures for infrastructure, data, and applications, as well as tagging and compliance practices. It supports well-architected application design across reliability, security, cost optimization, performance efficiency, and operational excellence.
